title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Ava Thompson
description:
Motivation: Reduce per-token inference cost for common production workloads with minimal developer changes. This PR implements (1) safer, workload-aware defaults for batching and KV/prefix caching, (2) an automated quantization-profile selector with conservative fallbacks, and (3) initial unit-economics tooling (CLI + service endpoints + dashboard hooks) to estimate cost impact for different configurations. Summary of changes: - Defaults: introduce 'autotune_defaults' config that sets initial batch_size/window, cache TTLs, and batching strategy based on observed latency percentiles and sequence-length histograms. The goal is low-friction improvements for existing customers while enabling opt-outs. - Quant profiles: add a quant_profile registry and selector that picks target quantization (fp16/int8/q4_0) per-model+workload based on historical accuracy regressions recorded in evals. Provides runtime fallback to higher-precision model variant on quality regressions. - Unit-econ tooling: new endpoint /internal/unit_econ/estimate plus CLI 'redwood autotune estimate' that computes expected cost/latency given a sample workload and candidate configs. Dashboard hooks emit per-route projected savings. Rollout strategy: feature-flagged, rollout in canaries (10%) for 72h before ramping to 100% contingent on SLOs. Results from internal perf runs: 8-14% aggregate cost reduction on mixed workload (median 11%), up to 28% for short-sequence chat scenarios; <2% latency regression at p95 for most configs. Checklist: - [x] implement autotune_defaults config and runtime integration - [x] quant_profile registry and selector - [x] unit-econ service + CLI + dashboard events - [x] end-to-end tests and perf canary harness - [x] documentation and upgrade notes - [x] feature flag + rollout plan

Related: ENG-4231 for metric/alert work, ENG-4312 for quant evaluation harness. See docs/cost-optimization.md for operator-facing details.

review_comments: Diego Martinez (reviewer): Can you clarify how the default TTL for KV cache was chosen? It looked aggressive for our high-cardinality routes.

Ava Thompson (author): TTL is now heuristic: for routes with >10k unique prefixes we prefer shorter TTLs and rely more on batching; updated description and comments in cache_manager.go to explain the heuristic.
Priya Shah (reviewer): We need a clear opt-out path for enterprise customers who want to manage quantization manually. Please add a organization-level override.
Ava Thompson (author): Added org-level override config in autotune_defaults and documented in docs/cost-optimization.md.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Unit-econ estimates are useful but I'd prefer a confidence band; can the CLI output p10/p90 estimates?
Ava Thompson (author): CLI now reports median and p10/p90 based on sampled latency distribution (see unit_econ/service.py). Added tests for distribution-based estimates.
Priya Shah (approver): Approved — minor nit on log message formatting addressed in follow-up commit.
Diego Martinez (approver): Approved — perf numbers look good in canary, no regressions observed after 48h.
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV caching, a quantization profile selector with safe fallbacks, and initial unit-economics tooling (CLI + service + dashboard hooks). Expected to reduce per-token cost by ~10% on mixed workloads. Feature gated and rolled out via canary.
notes_for_ops: Feature flags: deploy autotune_flags.yaml to canary first. Monitor route-level cost projections (unit_econ.*) and p95 latency. Org overrides available via autotune_defaults.org_overrides. Rollback: flip feature flag to disable_autotune and revert config. See docs/cost-optimization.md for detailed steps.
manual_steps: Run perf canary: scripts/benchmarks/run_autotune_bench.sh against canary cluster
Notify customers on Dedicated plan about new defaults via release notes template
Schedule 24h post-rollout review to validate unit-econ projections
